$comment: Week Aqua (model code 5746) Bluetooth test vectors, read by the iOS app's tests (apps/ios/AquaTomeKit/Tests/WeekAquaTests) and meant for the site's too, so both send the same bytes. Change both implementations together. From the hands-on tests with the owner's three lights and the WEEK AQUA capture of 2026-11-03 (docs/research/aquarium-device-control.md). Light names and addresses are synthetic: never put a real device's name suffix or address here. Times are the phone's local time. WEEK AQUA also sends `F9 55 55 55 55 55 55 55` on connecting; its meaning is unknown and it is never sent.

gatt.note: Write fff2 under fff0, without response; fff1 never sends anything. The firmware-update service f000ffc0 is never written to: only fff0 is looked for.

write.note: the same in the long form
a firmware-update characteristic listed under fff0: never

advert.name: WEEKAQUA3.0

clock.note: the phone's local time, hour, minute and second in BCD

levels.note: blue only, confirmed by eye on each light
off, confirmed by eye on each light
the owner's group, as WEEK AQUA sent it: Green at half brightness

manual.note: manual mode: applies the levels and timer written before it. alokauz's 8 bytes; the research notes write it FD F1

timer.note: the owner's timer, captured from WEEK AQUA: past midnight, on almost all day
the timer the lights were seen to switch off by; the hands-on test sent 00 in the seventh byte, WEEK AQUA sends 01 for a window this long

brightness.note: each rounded to the nearest step, a half up; WEEK AQUA's own half brightness sent 54 114 57 117

write.note: the order the lights took, which is also how WEEK AQUA leaves them: clock, manual, levels, timer, manual. The owner's group put back as it was.
